title: Alice & Bob Accelerates Modular Cat-Qubit Roadmap to 200 Logical Qubits from 3,600 Physical Qubits by 2030 - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Alice & Bob doubled its 2030 target to 200 logical qubits from 3,600 physical cat qubits (Carbon, nine linked modules), scaling to 2,048 logical qubits by 2034 (Neon) aimed at RSA-2048 and Bitcoin cryptographic stress testing; cat qubits' native bit-flip suppression cuts the physical-to-logical overhead.

insights.claim: Because superconducting cat qubits autonomously suppress bit-flip errors in hardware, Alice & Bob's architecture concentrates error-correction overhead on phase-flip errors, substantially reducing the physical-to-logical qubit ratio needed for fault tolerance.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An 18:1 physical-to-logical ratio (3,600 to 200) is far lower than typical surface-code estimates, a key differentiator if it holds.
insights.locator: Paris- and Boston-based quantum computing company

insights.claim: Alice & Bob's 2030 Carbon system targets 200 logical qubits from 3,600 physical cat qubits, double its previous 2030 logical-qubit target.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Accelerated roadmap raises the bar for competing fault-tolerance timelines; watch delivery on 2026 Helium and 2028 Beryllium milestones.
insights.locator: Paris- and Boston-based quantum computing company

insights.claim: Alice & Bob's roadmap: Helium (2026) prototype logical qubit demonstrating active QEC; Beryllium (2028) 6 logical qubits with fault-tolerant universality; Carbon (2030) 200 logical qubits over 9 modules; Oxygen (2032) 1,024 logical qubits over 25 modules; Neon (2034) 2,048 logical qubits over 56 modules.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Concrete dated milestones allow tracking of execution risk.
insights.locator: Alice & Bob 2026–2034 Modular Fault-Tolerant Quantum Roadmap

insights.claim: Alice & Bob says its 2030 Carbon system would unlock Ising and Hubbard materials simulations, and its 2032 Oxygen system would enable initial Shor algorithm implementations and complex chemistry such as FeMoCo.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Defines when commercially relevant materials and chemistry use cases might arrive on this platform.
insights.locator: Alice & Bob 2026–2034 Modular Fault-Tolerant Quantum Roadmap

insights.claim: Alice & Bob's 2034 Neon system with 2,048 logical qubits is positioned to support RSA-2048 and Bitcoin cryptographic stress testing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A named vendor timeline of ~2034 for RSA-2048/Bitcoin-relevant capability sharpens the post-quantum migration clock for crypto assets.
insights.quote: Supports RSA-2048 and Bitcoin cryptographic stress testing
insights.locator: Alice & Bob 2026–2034 Modular Fault-Tolerant Quantum Roadmap

insights.claim: AI-assisted chip design and algorithmic optimizations have cut Alice & Bob's estimated RSA-2048 resource requirements by a factor of 40.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Falling resource estimates for breaking RSA compress cryptographic risk timelines independent of hardware progress.

insights.claim: Alice & Bob's 2030 Carbon architecture will occupy 350 square meters and link nine dilution refrigerators via cryogenic coaxial cables that exchange Bell pairs across chips without degrading quantum states.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Multi-fridge modularity creates demand for dilution refrigerators and cryogenic interconnects.

insights.claim: Alice & Bob's Carbon system is designed around degree-five qubit connectivity, a hybrid LDPC and repetition error-correction code, a 10-microsecond clock speed, 10 million logical operations and a target logical error rate of 10−7.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Specs allow apples-to-apples comparison with other fault-tolerance roadmaps (e.g., logical ops and error rates).

insights.claim: Alice & Bob's modular multi-cryostat design bypasses single-fridge scaling limits through standardized QPU manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Standardized modules imply manufacturing-driven scaling economics rather than bespoke giant systems.

insights.claim: Alice & Bob's accelerated schedule builds on milestones under France's PROQCIMA program, where it fabricated, assembled and operated three independent quantum processors and demonstrated all core logical-qubit building blocks near the error-correction threshold.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: French state program funding is a key backer; PROQCIMA milestones are a de-risking signal.
